findings.summary: Every clean-install Whop checkout will FAIL the primary /desktop/connect-from-checkout call because the backend endpoint is gated by require_internal_secret (x-internal-secret header) — a server-side secret that CANNOT be embedded in the desktop's browser JS. All users hit the email-fallback path silently, dressed as if the primary path worked.
findings.evidence: WelcomeRoute.tsx:407-420 fetches (base ?? 'https://api.liquidclips.app') + '/desktop/connect-from-checkout' with body {clerk_user_id, whop_membership_id, email} · zero x-internal-secret header. Backend at junior-backend/app/routes/desktop.py:194-198 declares `_internal: Annotated[bool, Depends(require_internal_secret)] = True`. deps.py:88-91 raises 401 'invalid internal secret' when header missing (in production INTERNAL_API_SECRET is set). The account-app companion route account-app/src/app/api/desktop/connect-whop-checkout/route.ts:57-67 shows the canonical path: server-side proxy that adds `x-internal-secret: process.env.INTERNAL_API_SECRET ?? ''`. Desktop is a Tauri browser context — cannot hold that secret. Result: every prod clean install hits the catch at WelcomeRoute:438 → setActivationError → user sees 'Card on file · check your email for a sign-in ID from Liquid Clips. Paste it…' fallback. The InlineWhopCheckout onComplete promise-of-inline-activation is a lie in prod.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'require_internal_secret' junior-backend/app/routes/desktop.py && grep -n 'x-internal-secret' desktop-2/src/design-os/routes/WelcomeRoute.tsx && grep -rn 'x-internal-secret' desktop-2/src/ | grep -v test
findings.suggested_fix: Two clean paths: (a) route the desktop call through account-app (via a deep link or a hosted redirect that carries the Clerk session cookie), matching the existing /api/desktop/connect-whop-checkout proxy pattern. (b) Add a dedicated backend endpoint (e.g. /desktop/connect-from-checkout-public) that authenticates by validating the Whop membership_id server-side against Whop's API + short-lived nonce minted at checkout complete, rather than internal secret. Do NOT try to embed INTERNAL_API_SECRET in the client. If keeping the email fallback as the shipping path is intended, DELETE the inline fetch and simply show the fallback copy after Whop onComplete + tell users to check email — don't lie about the primary path working.

findings.summary: Silent-success lie · try/catch around handleActivationUrl treats no-throw as success, but activation.ts documents 'Never throws · all failure paths route through the state machine'. User pastes an invalid JWT/challenge → catch never fires → markWelcomeAcked('recovered') + onDone() unconditionally close the LoginScreen. User lands in the app un-authenticated with a bad JWT, next /sync 401s, they get bounced back with no signal about what went wrong.
findings.evidence: handleActivationUrl in lib/activation.ts:368 emits({status:'failed',error}) and returns early on parse-error (:374-378), challenge-mismatch (:391-397), and JWT-store-error (:408-414). Never throws for any user-visible failure mode. WelcomeRoute.tsx:484-499 wraps in try/catch expecting throws. Line 488 await returns → line 489 fires paste_code_succeeded telemetry, line 490 markWelcomeAcked('recovered'), line 491 onDone(). The App-level WelcomeGate at App.tsx:340 sets acked=true → unmounts LoginScreen → user is in-app with no valid JWT.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'never throws\|Never throws\|emit({[[:space:]]*status: "failed"' desktop-2/src/lib/activation.ts && grep -n 'await handleActivationUrl' desktop-2/src/design-os/routes/WelcomeRoute.tsx
findings.suggested_fix: After `await handleActivationUrl(url)`, inspect the outcome: `const snap = getActivationSnapshot(); if (snap.status !== 'activated') { setPasteError(snap.error ?? 'Activation failed'); setPhase('picking'); return; }` before calling markWelcomeAcked + onDone. Same pattern must be applied to onWhopCheckoutComplete at line 432 (the fetch throw is caught but the subsequent handleActivationUrl silent-failure path is not guarded).

findings.summary: Same silent-success lie in the Whop checkout completion path · after connect-from-checkout returns license_jwt, code does `await handleActivationUrl(activationUrl); markWelcomeAcked; onDone` with no post-await activation-state inspection. If the JWT is malformed / challenge-mismatch (challengeless path uses TRUSTED_CHALLENGELESS_SOURCES.has('whop-checkout') so this specific path should bypass — but a mistyped source query or expired token still lands here), user acks welcome + closes login while never actually activating.
findings.evidence: WelcomeRoute.tsx:431-437 builds activationUrl='liquidclips://activate?token=<jwt>&source=whop-checkout' → await handleActivationUrl → markWelcomeAcked(signInMode) → bus.emit('mode:set') → onDone(). Zero inspection of getActivationSnapshot() between the await and the ack. handleActivationUrl.ts:373 emits({status:'activating',error:null}) which can transition to 'failed' before returning. Guarded by TRUSTED_CHALLENGELESS_SOURCES check at :387-388 but JWT-store or backend /sync auth-fail (:462) still emit failed.
findings.reproduce: Same as P1-001 · additionally: modify the license_jwt returned by connect-from-checkout to be a malformed 3-segment string (fake JWT) · observe the ack fires despite no valid JWT written.
findings.suggested_fix: Identical to P1-001: check snapshot.status after await. Add a post-condition inline test: `if (!hasJwt()) { setActivationError('Activation completed but license not stored · re-open Whop link.'); return; }`.

findings.summary: useMemo used for side-effect · captureColdLeadFromUrl() writes localStorage inside a useMemo hook. React's contract explicitly says memo bodies must be pure. Strict Mode may double-invoke (harmless here — writes are idempotent) but Concurrent Mode may skip / re-run at any time — the pattern is fragile.
findings.evidence: Line 284 `useMemo(() => captureColdLeadFromUrl(), []);` — no returned value, ignored. Function writes to window.localStorage on line 89. Immediately followed at line 285 by `const cold = useMemo<ColdLeadContext | null>(() => readColdLead(), []);` which reads that same localStorage. Order-dependent side-effect coupling via memo bodies is a karpathy-guidelines anti-pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the capture to a top-level useEffect(() => { captureColdLeadFromUrl(); }, []) OR call it inline before the useState/useMemo hooks fire on module load (via a top-of-component `useRef` guard: `if (!ranOnce.current) { ranOnce.current = true; captureColdLeadFromUrl(); }`). Cold-lead read on the same tick would then need to re-read after — cleanest: combine into a single useMemo that captures-then-reads and returns the ColdLeadContext value.

findings.summary: 16 concurrent muted-autoPlay <video> decoders with NO preload attribute · default browser behavior is preload='auto' which starts streaming all 8 unique MP4s (~5-11MB) on mount. On slow connections this delays LoginScreen interactivity; on macOS 12+ WKWebView this stresses the frame decoder pipeline (measured 16 tiles doubled from 8 unique clips × 246px × 432px).
findings.evidence: WelcomeRoute.tsx:678-688 <video src={c.url} muted autoPlay playsInline loop /> — no preload attr. BUNDLED_CLIPS has 8 unique URLs (some duplicate at index 0 + 7 both reference /demos/03-money-moment.mp4). Marquee track doubles them → 16 <video> nodes. Sum of demo MP4s: 510+906+1152+361+359+692+474 ≈ 4.4MB unique + 1152KB double-count of 03 = ~5.5MB min. On first mount before HQ /hq/carousel/clips fetch replaces the list, all 16 decoders start.
findings.suggested_fix: Add preload='metadata' to each <video> (still autoplays when in-viewport but doesn't pre-download full body). Alternatively wrap the video element in an IntersectionObserver that plays only tiles within the visible marquee window. For the marquee CSS animation running at 50s linear, only ~3-4 tiles are visible on a 900px right column at any time — the other 12 are decoding invisibly.

findings.summary: Docstring promise unmet · State B design promise 'carousel targets the lead's preview MP4 (from cold-email)' is captured/persisted via cold?.preview_clip_url but never rendered. Marquee always uses BUNDLED_CLIPS or HQ /hq/carousel/clips response. Cold-lead's specific preview URL is dead data.
findings.evidence: Docstring lines 10-11 explicitly say 'State B · cold-traffic lead ... Left → carousel targets the lead's preview MP4 (from cold-email)'. ColdLeadContext interface at :62-68 declares preview_clip_url?: string. captureColdLeadFromUrl reads it from ?d param (:78) and merges (:86). grep 'preview_clip_url' returns only these two lines — zero read sites in render.
findings.suggested_fix: In State B rendering, prepend a dedicated 'your preview' tile at index 0 of the marquee track OR replace BUNDLED_CLIPS[0] when cold.preview_clip_url is set. Alternatively, delete the preview_clip_url capture code + amend the docstring so the code and docs agree.

findings.summary: fetchHqClips has no timeout · a hung network on /hq/carousel/clips leaves the fetch pending indefinitely. If HQ ever returns a slow response (or the endpoint doesn't exist yet — no route named /hq/carousel/clips found in junior-backend), the request sits open. Cancelled flag prevents state update but the socket stays open until browser default (60s+).
findings.evidence: Line 237 `const r = await fetch(url.toString(), { headers: { accept: 'application/json' } });` — no signal / AbortController / timeout. Backend grep: `grep -rn '/hq/carousel/clips\|carousel/clips' junior-backend/app/` will help confirm whether the endpoint even exists (see reproduce). Non-fatal for LoginScreen (bundled fallback shows immediately) but leaves a dangling request per every mount + is an unaudited karpathy 'missing timeout on async' pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `const controller = new AbortController(); const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 3500); fetch(url.toString(), { signal: controller.signal, headers: {...} }).finally(() => clearTimeout(timeout));`. Bump the cancelled cleanup to also call controller.abort() to release the socket.

findings.summary: Dead pinning state · `const [backdropPinned] = useState(false);` — setter destructured out, no code path ever sets pinned=true, but the docstring at :271-272 promises 'fires when the user manually clicks a tile — implicit "I want this"'. Rotation timer at :306 checks backdropPinned unnecessarily.
findings.evidence: Line 274 declares state without exposing setter. Line 307 reads it but nothing writes it. Comment 271-272 documents behavior that never fires.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire the setter (add an onClick handler on the backdrop that calls setBackdropPinned(true) + persists to localStorage) OR delete the state + the pinning check + the misleading comment. Prefer delete — pin-on-click adds a modality the login screen doesn't need.

findings.summary: Persistent document-level capture-phase click listener · although the handler exits early after audioUnlockedRef.current becomes true, the listener stays registered for the lifetime of the LoginScreen. Every click during State C checkout (buttons in the Whop iframe, if any bubble) hits this handler first. Zero functional impact because handler doesn't call stop/preventDefault, but it's an unnecessary hot-path on every click.
findings.evidence: Line 347 addEventListener('click', unlockOnFirstGesture, { capture: true }) with no once:true. Line 350-351 removeEventListener runs only on unmount (whole LoginScreen unmounts). Handler at 342-346: checks ref, returns early after first unlock — but function call itself + capture-phase dispatch cost remain per click.
findings.suggested_fix: After the first unlock inside unlockOnFirstGesture, self-removeListener: `document.removeEventListener('click', unlockOnFirstGesture, { capture: true }); document.removeEventListener('keydown', unlockOnFirstGesture, { capture: true });`. Removes the hot-path handler once its purpose is served.

findings.summary: Mobile @media specificity vs State C · grid-template-columns override at :1083 (1fr) conflicts with [data-state='checkout'] (1fr 0 0) at :826. Attribute selector wins → mobile checkout still renders phantom 0-width columns 2+3. Cosmetic only (children display:none anyway), but confusing.
findings.evidence: Base @900px: grid-template-columns: 1fr, single column. State C: grid-template-columns: 1fr 0 0. When both apply (mobile + checkout), specificity 0,1,1 (attribute) > 0,1,0 (element), attribute selector wins → 1fr 0 0. No harmful effect but not what the code visibly says.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit mobile State C rule: `@media (max-width:900px) { .lc-login-root[data-state='checkout'] { grid-template-columns: 1fr } }`. Trivial, cosmetic.

findings.summary: Fake-precision social-proof number · clipperCount = clips.length × 87 produces a plausibly-precise number (e.g. 696 for 8 clips, 8700 for 100 clips) that scales linearly with a display constant. Any observer with two page loads sees the number update in strict multiples of 87.
findings.evidence: Line 370 `const clipperCount = useMemo(() => clips.length * 87, [clips.length]);`. Renders at :700 as '{clipperCount.toLocaleString()} clippers'. If HQ returns 12 clips, number reads '1,044 clippers'; if 15, '1,305 clippers'. Karpathy 'hidden assumption not surfaced' — the number pretends to be real but derives from a display-side multiplier.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) fetch a real total-clipper count from HQ (add a `clippers` field to /hq/carousel/clips response) and fall back to a fixed number when unavailable, or (b) delete the count entirely and lead with the $-paid-last-week number which comes from real earningsCents. Fake precision undermines the 'proof before ask' framing in the docstring at line 28.

findings.summary: BUNDLED_CLIPS[0] and BUNDLED_CLIPS[7] both reference /demos/03-money-moment.mp4 · 8 tiles show only 7 unique videos. Doubled marquee has 4 copies of the same clip. Not a bug but hurts the 'proof' illusion — attentive users see repetition every 3-4 tiles.
findings.evidence: Line 186: { url: '/demos/03-money-moment.mp4', handle: '@clipsbyava', ... }. Line 192: { url: '/demos/03-money-moment.mp4', handle: '@nova.cuts', ... }. Only 7 unique .mp4 files exist under public/demos/ (verified: 01-clipping through 07-cold-email-preview).
findings.suggested_fix: Either ship an 8th unique demo mp4 (recommended — Uncle Daniel bench already produces these) or reduce BUNDLED_CLIPS to 7 (drop line 192). At 246px tile width + 24px gap, 7 tiles = 1,890px, still enough to cover a 1440px right column with 1.3× overlap for the marquee loop.

findings.summary: isColdLead-driven docstring promises State B copy 'single-CTA discipline · Sign-in CTA · discount code slot' but the actual State B branch shares its recovery <details> block with State A · discount code slot is present in both states. Docstring/code drift is minor but the 'single-CTA discipline' claim is technically false since the recovery form is a secondary hidden CTA.
findings.evidence: Docstring line 30 'Single-CTA discipline (State B has 1 CTA · State A has 2)'. But the recovery <details> at :628-649 renders unconditionally (below the state-A/state-B conditional). State B thus shows: 1 primary CTA + 1 collapsed-details recovery form. Same shape as State A's 2 primary + 1 collapsed recovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Update docstring to say 'single primary CTA + collapsed recovery' or move the recovery <details> inside the isColdLead branch and hide entirely in State B (cold leads have already been identified — a discount code is redundant). Prefer update-the-docstring; the collapsed recovery is a valuable escape hatch.

ransom_paywall_trigger_1.scope: Trigger #1 of ransom-paywall pattern (Max · 2026-07-06). Focus is ARCHITECTURE + PATTERN generalisation — findings that will replicate to triggers #2-#6 unless fixed at the primitive.

smoke_tests_run.name: grep AssetRansomPaywall consumers
smoke_tests_run.output: Only PublishModule imports the paywall today. Trigger #2-#6 not yet wired — confirmed vs MAX_HANDOFF_RANSOM_PAYWALL_2026-07-06.md §7.

findings.summary: Stale-closure race after Whop unlock — publishNow re-invoked with tier still === 'clipper' → guard re-trips and paywall may reopen or no-op.
findings.evidence: handleComplete() at AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:133-142 awaits me.reload() (which synchronously updates the module-cache in useMe.ts and calls emit() → listener.setTick), THEN awaits props.onUnlocked(). React does NOT synchronously flush external-store setState between these two awaits — no browser paint happens. props.onUnlocked was defined at PublishModule.tsx:550 during a render where tier.tier === 'clipper' and its closure references THAT render's publishNow (deps: [exportState, slug, publishAction, tier.tier] at :516). When onUnlocked runs its `await publishNow()` at :554, that publishNow closure still gates on `tier.tier === 'clipper' && isGuestQuotaExhausted()` at :486. Quota was NOT decremented (decrement fires only on success at :514, which never ran because publishNow tripped the gate this iteration). Net effect: guard trips again → setRansomOpen(true) is a no-op (already true, but the earlier setRansomOpen(false) at :551 was ALSO queued in the same microtask) — final state is undefined-order between the two React updates.
findings.reproduce: 1. localStorage.setItem('lc:guest-mode','1'); localStorage.setItem('lc:guest-clips-remaining','0'); 2. Force tier === 'clipper' via useMe cache. 3. Click Export in PublishModule. 4. Paywall opens. 5. Complete Whop checkout in dev sandbox. 6. Observe: paywall dismisses but export never fires OR paywall visibly flashes closed→open. Instrument by console.log('onUnlocked-tier', tier.tier) inside the onUnlocked lambda at PublishModule.tsx:550 — will print 'clipper' post-unlock.
findings.suggested_fix: Two options — architecture is the choice for the sibling wraps: (A) push the gate INSIDE publishAction/runExportAndMint so it re-reads tier via useTierCaps().tier at invoke time (not via closed-over prop). Requires refactoring runExportAndMint to accept a tier snapshot arg OR reading from a ref that mirrors tier.tier. (B) Have onUnlocked skip the deflection guard by passing a `forceThrough: true` flag to publishNow that bypasses the ransom gate for one call. Option B is cheaper and copy-pasteable to all 6 triggers — each trigger's onUnlocked passes `{ skipRansomGate: true }` to the underlying action.

findings.summary: Price copy lies — '$0 today · $99.99/mo after' but WHOP_FOUNDER_PLAN_ID (plan_NMKvKj8SVVKsY) is doc'd as '$99.99/mo · immediate charge · no trial' in whopCheckout.ts:49-57.
findings.evidence: AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:168-170 renders literal '$0 today · $99.99/mo after · cancel anytime'. whopCheckout.ts:49-56 (unedited by Max) says: 'rotated from plan_svbzoXoT4oj6b (had a 365-day trial with card capture at signup — wrong model) to plan_NMKvKj8SVVKsY: $99.99/mo · immediate charge · no trial'. The paywall uses WHOP_FOUNDER_PLAN_ID directly at line 179 → user is charged $99.99 today, not $0.
findings.reproduce: Read whopCheckout.ts:49-57 comment · compare to AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:169 literal. Or: run a real Whop checkout with plan_NMKvKj8SVVKsY and observe immediate $99.99 charge.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (A) swap planId in the paywall to FREE_WITH_CARD_PLAN_ID (plan_1jtkUjUmHbaC3, the $0-today / $1-in-365d plan Max created — this is what the copy promises), OR (B) fix copy to '$99.99 today · monthly · cancel anytime · agency features unlocked'. Feedback_ship_blocker_discipline + feedback_use_brand_assets both make this a hard ship-block. Voice-check per feedback_voice_no_bounty_use_skill — 19yo clippers expecting $0 will churn hard when Whop shows $99.99. Pattern-critical: whichever copy you land here will be templated across all 6 triggers.

findings.summary: Paywall bypasses ModalPortal — no body scroll-lock, dual Esc handlers, position:fixed against transformed ancestor risk.
findings.evidence: AssetRansomPaywall renders inline in PublishModule's tree via a Fragment (PublishModule.tsx:542) — does NOT call useModalPortal()/useRegisterModal()/createPortal. Consequences: (1) no scroll-lock on body (ModalPortal.tsx:61-75 handles this) — user can scroll cockpit behind the paywall; (2) TWO Esc listeners fire on 'Escape' (the paywall's window-level listener at :118 does e.preventDefault() but not e.stopPropagation() — ModalPortal's window listener at ModalPortal.tsx:79 also fires and would close any layered modal beneath); (3) position:fixed at CSS:12 resolves relative to nearest transformed ancestor per the CSS spec — the paywall is a great-grandchild of section.lc-cd-mod which itself is inside cockpit shells that may apply transforms during animations. ModalPortal.tsx:105-121 was created explicitly to solve this via createPortal(document.body). Pattern-critical because triggers #2-6 will inherit this hazard AND may be mounted from deeper trees (thumbnail from editor, watermark from export flow).
findings.reproduce: 1. Open trigger #1 via reproduce recipe above. 2. Scroll wheel over the cockpit area behind the paywall — cockpit scrolls (should be locked). 3. If any other modal is open behind (e.g. SubmitToWhopModal), press Esc — both close simultaneously.
findings.suggested_fix: Refactor AssetRansomPaywall to (a) call useModalPortal() and createPortal into that host, (b) use useRegisterModal({ id: `ransom/${trigger}`, open: isOpen, onEscape: onDismiss }) for the Esc stack, (c) drop the window-level keydown listener except for the Tab focus trap. Land this before rolling to 5 sibling triggers — fixes 6 hazards for the cost of 1.

findings.summary: AssetPreview.src can be empty string when focusedClip has neither vertical_path nor cut_path — silent broken preview.
findings.evidence: PublishModule.tsx:546 constructs the assetPreview as `{ kind: 'video', src: focusedClip.vertical_path ?? focusedClip.cut_path ?? '' }`. When both are null, src='' — <video> element renders with empty src → silent black frame or browser-specific error. AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:210-220 RansomAssetPreview renders the <video> unconditionally. In practice publishNow returns early at :469-477 for missing slug, but there's no guard on missing paths — a project with slug but no exported clip could still trigger the paywall via a race.
findings.reproduce: Force focusedClip to `{ idx: 0, vertical_path: null, cut_path: null, thumbnails: [] }` in dev. Open paywall. Inspect DOM: <video src='' loop autoplay>.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AssetPreview discriminated union with a `{ kind: 'placeholder'; label: string }` variant. In PublishModule, when both paths are null, pass the placeholder variant (e.g. label='Your finished clip'). Pattern-critical: siblings for thumbnail-download (single PNG src) and custom-caption-export (styled overlay) will have similar empty-source failure modes — bake the null-handling into RansomAssetPreview once.

findings.summary: z-index collision: paywall root and .lc-toast both at 200 → order-of-DOM decides stacking → toast fired inside paywall (e.g. Whop error) may render behind the paywall.
findings.evidence: AssetRansomPaywall.css:14 sets .lc-ransom-root z-index:200. index.css:1453 sets .lc-toast z-index:200 (same layer). Higher layers exist (InboxSheet 9000, DemoOverlay 800, InAppBrowser 400, SyncMailMoneyDrop 400) that would render OVER the paywall — the user could open Inbox from a HUD affordance during checkout and lose sight of the paywall entirely. Toasts stacking at the same z-index means DOM order decides — toasts are typically appended late to a portal container that's a later sibling of body children, so they'd RENDER OVER the paywall; but if the paywall itself emits a toast via bus.emit from the WhopCheckoutEmbed's onComplete failure path, both siblings compete unpredictably.
findings.reproduce: grep -rn 'z-index' desktop-2/src --include='*.css' | sort. Note AssetRansomPaywall=200, .lc-toast=200, InboxSheet=9000.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt a documented z-index scale in index.css (currently ad-hoc). Recommend: modals=1000, paywall=1100 (paywall must beat other modals since it deflects them), toast=1200 (must beat modals to communicate their state), inbox=9000 stays. Bake the paywall layer into a --lc-z-paywall CSS var so all 6 triggers share.

findings.summary: Focus trap breaks when WhopCheckoutEmbed rehydrates its iframe — focusables snapshot is stale, and iframe-internal focus escapes the trap entirely.
findings.evidence: The trap at :96-99 queries focusables ONCE on mount and captures them in the effect closure. When WhopCheckoutEmbed's iframe mounts/reloads (checkout has multiple states — email → card → confirm), the focusables inside change dramatically, but the trap loop still cycles based on the initial snapshot. Worse: focus INSIDE an iframe is opaque to the parent document — document.activeElement returns the <iframe> element itself, so `document.activeElement === first` never matches while the user is typing card details. Real behavior: Shift+Tab from card fields may escape to the cockpit behind the scrim. restore-focus at :121 targets previouslyFocusedRef (the Export button on PublishModule) which is FINE for dismiss/unlock, but during checkout an unmount from a WhopCheckout error path could restore focus to a button that's rendering a re-invoke of publishNow → immediately re-fires the trigger.
findings.reproduce: Open paywall in dev, click into Whop's card field, press Shift+Tab repeatedly — observe focus escape ring appear on cockpit elements behind the scrim.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebuild the focusables list on a MutationObserver watching dialogRef.current, OR (simpler) add a `.lc-ransom-modal` inert scroll-region + aria-hidden the cockpit siblings so any escape into them is invisible to AT and inert to clicks. Copy the desktop/ ModalPortal pattern that already solves this for InlineWhopCheckout.

findings.summary: Guest quota decrement is not idempotent + fires on partial success (mint failed / campaign missing) → user gets under-charged clips or double-decremented on retry.
findings.evidence: publishAction.fire() at :490 returns null on any thrown error inside runExportAndMint. runExportAndMint throws in several partial-success paths: 'campaign_not_found' (:407), 'campaign_no_whop_reward_id' (:416). In these cases the EXPORT succeeded (base MP4 written to disk at :284) and the toast at :404/:411 confirms partial success, but result===null triggers the exportState='error' path at :492-507 AND skips the decrementGuestClipsRemaining() call at :514. User successfully created a paid-tier-worthy asset but their quota was not decremented — silently receives >10 free clips. Conversely, if the user hits Export again after a network hiccup that logged mint success but returned null, they double-decrement.
findings.reproduce: Force activeCampaignId to a slug that doesn't exist in seed. Trigger publishNow. Observe: MP4 lands on disk, toast says 'Publish tracked (partial)', quota unchanged. Repeat 20 times → user has 20 free-tier clips instead of 10.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the decrement to fire on ANY export success (before the mint step), OR make the runner return a structured result `{ exported: boolean; minted: boolean }` and decide based on `exported`. Pattern-critical: siblings will have similar 'partial success' shapes (thumb download success + gallery cache-write failure, watermark removal success + upload failure). Bake success-vs-mint separation into the audit-action contract once.

findings.summary: FREE_WITH_CARD_PLAN_ID + CHECKOUT_URL exports have no consumer in desktop-2/src — dead public API.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'FREE_WITH_CARD_PLAN_ID\|FREE_WITH_CARD_CHECKOUT_URL' /Users/dipdip/code/jnr/desktop-2/src → 1 hit (declaration only). Handoff note says LoginScreen (claude-app lane) will consume it. Not a lint fail today but risks becoming stale drift if claude-app renames/replaces the constant.
findings.suggested_fix: Either mark with a `// consumed by: <file>` doc pointer OR gate export behind a claude-app-owned barrel and re-export only once actually wired. If RP-P0-002 fix routes the paywall itself through FREE_WITH_CARD_PLAN_ID, this concern evaporates.

findings.summary: Copy dictionary uses 'clip' + 'earning' — no banned-word violations. Tone is 90% right; two lines could over-promise.
findings.evidence: Reviewed each headline/sub against feedback_voice_no_bounty_use_skill (no 'bounty' — pass) and against 19yo clipper vocabulary. Two minor drifts: (1) 'earn-publish' sub says '50% MRR line stays yours' — 'MRR' is SaaS-founder jargon, will read as opaque to a 19yo. Suggest '50% of the payout stays yours' or '50% of what this clip earns'. (2) 'schedule-confirm' says 'Cancel anytime.' immediately after 'Confirm to lock the time.' — mixed signal (locked but cancel-able). Suggest just 'Lock the time or change it later.'
findings.suggested_fix: Two-line copy edit. Trivial. Won't block ship but improves conversion probability.

findings.summary: WhopCheckoutEmbed onComplete signature drift vs InlineWhopCheckout — receipt args discarded.
findings.evidence: InlineWhopCheckout.tsx:79-84 receives (receivedPlanId, receiptId) from onComplete and forwards a receipt object to its parent. AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:182 does `onComplete={() => { void handleComplete(); }}` — discards both args. Not a bug today (backend webhook is source of truth for the receipt), but the two consumers of WhopCheckoutEmbed drift on this contract. Any future audit that needs the receiptId in an analytics tick would have to touch AssetRansomPaywall.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a receiptId param to onUnlocked so the paywall can forward Whop's opaque receipt to the parent for telemetry, OR document explicitly with a comment 'receipt intentionally discarded · backend webhook resolves membership'. Pattern-critical for the 5 siblings — pick one contract.

pattern_generalisability_notes.roll_out_readiness: NOT READY for triggers #2-#6. RP-P0-001 (stale-closure race) and RP-P1-003 (bypass of ModalPortal) will replicate as-is to all 5 siblings and multiply the fix cost 6x. Fix the primitive once here.
pattern_generalisability_notes.props_shape: AssetRansomPaywallProps is clean — trigger discriminant + assetPreview union + onUnlocked/onDismiss/isOpen. Would benefit from an optional receiptId in onUnlocked (RP-P2-010) so telemetry can flow.
pattern_generalisability_notes.state_ownership: Correct — each trigger site owns its ransomOpen state. Confirmed no shared global. Pattern scales.
pattern_generalisability_notes.error_handling: Weakest link. handleComplete swallows me.reload() errors silently at AssetRansomPaywall.tsx:135-137. Non-fatal comment says onUnlocked will re-fetch, but onUnlocked in PublishModule doesn't re-fetch — it just calls publishNow which uses the stale tier closure (RP-P0-001). Recommend surfacing the reload error via bus.emit('toast', ...) so the user sees WHY publish didn't fire.
pattern_generalisability_notes.sibling_wiring_hazards: Triggers #2-#6 each need their own guest-quota-equivalent for the free tier. Thumbnail-download probably reads a thumbnail-quota, watermark-removal is binary (paid vs unpaid — no quota), custom-caption-export is binary, schedule-confirm is binary, earn-publish reuses guest quota. RP-P1-007's under-count/double-count bug will multiply if each sibling implements its own decrement path — build a shared consumeGuestQuota(feature) helper.

ransom_paywall_trigger_1.verdict_rationale: 2 × P0 (stale-closure race post-unlock → user completes checkout but publish never fires; price copy lies → user promised $0 today gets charged $99.99). 5 × P1 (portal bypass · empty asset src · z-index collision · focus trap iframe hole · non-idempotent quota decrement) — all P1s are pattern-critical and will replicate to 5 sibling triggers unfixed. Per feedback_lens_hard_gate + Max's explicit brief 'Every P0/P1 you find here I'll fix once and inherit across triggers #2-#6' → BLOCK ships the pattern until at minimum RP-P0-001, RP-P0-002, RP-P1-003 are addressed at the primitive layer.
